title: cobble-pr-scratchpad-ravi
body:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for the tiny PR series (related to microbatch + KV cache eviction behavior). Not an official RFC; recording hypotheses, quick check commands, and follow-ups so I don't forget mid-context-switch.

Problem summary (observed):
- After landing microbatch change (PR-4321), a small subset of production traffic shows degraded tail latency spikes (~95th-99th) in short-seq workloads.
- Correlated with KV cache invalidation events and increased CPU on inference proxy.
- Repro locally only when batching enabled + prefix caching on, and when sequence_len <= 64 and concurrency bursts > 200 qps.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction policy interaction with batching: when batches include requests that hit stale kv entries we get cache thrash and lock contention.
2) Microbatch scheduling edge: coalescing delay increased queuing and causes head-of-line blocking on short requests.
3) Proxy deserialization path: microbatch introduces a code path that re-allocates buffers synchronously causing syscall spikes.
4) Metrics noise: real issue is unrelated but rollout coincided. Low confidence.

Immediate reproducibility steps (dev machine):
- Start runtime with BATCH_DEBUG=1, KV_TRACE=debug, set BATCH_MAX_TIME=8ms, BATCH_MIN_SIZE=4.
- Use load generator script: tools/loadgen/shortseq-burst.py --qps 250 --seq-len 32 --concurrency 300 --duration 120s.
- Capture perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 120; sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
- Tail logs: docker logs -f runtime | sed -n '1,200p' and grepping for "kv-evict" and "batch-coalesce"

Observations from local run (notes):
- See repeated "kv-evict: key not found" messages with 20-30ms latency spikes.
- Flamegraph shows cycles in runtime::kv::get -> mutex::lock where contention increases during burst windows.
- When disabling prefix caching, spike disappears (but cost increases).

Quick hacks to test (non-prod):
- Try bumping KV cache capacity by 2x: runtime config kv_cache_size=8192 -> measure.
- Switch eviction policy from LRU to CLOCK (experimental) and rerun.
- Force microbatch to cap per-worker pending requests to 128 instead of 256.
- Add shallow backoff on cache-miss path (10us) to reduce thundering herd.

Checklist for PR updates (if I change code):
- [ ] Add unit tests for kv access under concurrent batch join (mock scheduler + fake clock).
- [ ] Add integration test that simulates short-seq burst and asserts p95 p99 < target.
- [ ] Add telemetry metric for "kv_eviction_reason" (cold|mem_pressure|ttl) and surface in console.
- [ ] Document config knobs in runtime docs: batching.{min_size,max_time}, kv_cache_size, kv_eviction_policy.
- [ ] Add rollout plan: canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% with observability gates (p99 latency, error rate, eviction count).

Refactor ideas (medium-term):
- Decouple cache mutex from hot-path reads by using sharded locks and atomic epoch counters. Could reduce lock contention without changing semantics.
- Introduce a two-tier cache: tiny per-worker L1 for prefix hits + shared L2. L1 handles bursts with no contention.
- Rework microbatch scheduler to prefer short tasks first (SJF-ish) when predicted sequence_len < threshold to reduce head-of-line blocking. Need to weigh complexity vs fairness.

Follow-ups / async actions:
- File an observability ticket to add kv eviction breakdown in console (include sample query and dashboard mockup). (LINEAR-987)
- Try CLOCK eviction locally and collect p95/p99 delta (assign to Jun).
- If CLOCK works, spin up canary and monitor for 48h.
- Coordinate with SRE on safe rollout windows (avoid peak APAC times) and add automated rollback hook.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep experiments small and reversible. Document each config change in PR description.
- When writing tests, prefer deterministic fake-threads rather than sleeping; flakiness is death here.
- Discuss with Maya about adding a "short-seq" label in the routing layer so we can route known short requests to optimized pool.

Commands I used (snippets):
- tools/loadgen/shortseq-burst.py --endpoint http://localhost:8080/gen --qps 250 --seq-len 32 --concurrency 300 --duration 120s
- curl -sS http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_evict || true
- docker exec -it runtime bash -c 'grep -n "kv-evict" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 200'

Sticky open questions:
- Is the cache eviction count rising globally or only on specific model shards? Need per-shard telemetry.
- Does this surface for longer sequence lengths at different qps? Early testing says no but do systematic sweep.
- How do we balance cost (cache size) vs tail latency? Add a simple cost model to evaluate.

If I get a few free hours:
- Implement sharded locks PoC (one-week hack) and measure contention improvement.
- Build a synthetic benchmark that varies seq_len distribution so we can replay customer patterns in CI.

End notes:
- This file is a personal working doc. If anything here becomes a real proposal, I'll move it to /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime and create a short RFC.
- Save before context switch.

-- Ravi
